title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
prompt: There is one bookstore owner who has a store open for `n` minutes. Every minute, some number of customers enter the store, given by an array `customers` of length `n` where `customers[i]` is the number of customers entering at minute `i`, and all those customers leave at the end of that minute. On some minutes the owner is grumpy, given by a binary array `grumpy` of length `n` where `grumpy[i] == 1` means the owner is grumpy during minute `i`. When the owner is grumpy, the customers entering that minute do not become satisfied; otherwise they do. The bookstore owner knows a secret technique to keep themselves not grumpy for `minutes` consecutive minutes, but can only use it once. Return the maximum number of customers that can be satisfied throughout the day.

examples.explanation: The owner uses the technique during minutes 3 to 5 (customers 2,1,1), keeping those customers satisfied. Combined with the customers already satisfied when not grumpy (1+1+1+7=10), the total is 10 + (2+1+1) = 16.
The owner is never grumpy, so every customer is already satisfied regardless of where the technique is used

hints: Start by counting all customers who are already satisfied (minutes where grumpy is 0) — that's a fixed baseline regardless of where the technique is used.
The technique can only add the customers lost during a window of `minutes` consecutive grumpy minutes, so you want the window of size `minutes` that maximizes the number of otherwise-lost customers.
Use a fixed-size sliding window over the 'lost customers' values (customers[i] if grumpy[i] == 1 else 0), and track the best window sum; add that to the baseline satisfied count.

solution.approach: First compute the baseline of customers already satisfied when the owner isn't grumpy — this doesn't depend on where the technique is applied. Then, define the 'recoverable' customers at each minute as customers[i] if grumpy[i] is 1, else 0 (those are the ones lost that the technique could save). Slide a fixed-size window of length `minutes` over this recoverable array, tracking the maximum window sum with the standard running-sum technique. The answer is the baseline plus this maximum recoverable sum, since the best use of the one-time technique is over whichever window recovers the most otherwise-lost customers.
